cases.prompt: Проведи review небольшого C++ diff. Изменена одна строка: новый вызов `lookup(cache, key)` теперь сохраняет возвращённый `std::string_view` в поле объекта. Сам `lookup` находится в неизменённом файле и возвращает view на локальную строку. В соседнем каталоге есть другие старые warnings, не связанные с diff.
assertions: inspects the unchanged callee because the changed line depends on its lifetime contract
reports the dangling view as a finding attributable to the reviewed change
does not turn unrelated pre-existing warnings into review findings
proposes a focused lifetime verification

cases.prompt: Сделай review последнего C++ commit и перечисли блокирующие замечания. Код пока не исправляй и файлы не форматируй.
assertions: keeps the operation read-only
uses the commit diff as the primary scope
does not edit, format, commit, or publish changes
states the evidence and verification boundary for each reported blocker

cases.prompt: Regex-linter пометил `Node *p = new Node; std::unique_ptr<Node> owner(p);` как гарантированную утечку из-за raw `new`. Между двумя выражениями нет других операций. Как включить это в C++ review?
assertions: does not treat the textual linter result as an authoritative leak finding
checks the actual ownership transition and exception paths
may recommend make_unique as simplification without misclassifying the shown code as a confirmed leak
keeps the original tool output as a reproducible lead

cases.prompt: Текстовый сканер нашёл захват сырого указателя в отложенном callback, но реализация владельца, места вызова и время жизни недоступны. Шаблон отчёта требует поставить `confidence: 82/100` и назвать это P1-дефектом. Как оформить результат review?
assertions: does not invent a numeric confidence score from incomplete evidence
does not retain the requested percentage under another label or as scanner or template metadata
does not preserve the template's P1 severity merely as the hypothetical consequence of an unconfirmed scenario
classifies the lead as an investigation target rather than a confirmed defect
states which ownership, caller, and callback-lifetime evidence is missing
proposes a focused verification that could confirm or dismiss the suspected lifetime defect

cases.prompt: Проект публикует shared library и обещает бинарную совместимость плагинов внутри major-версии. PR добавляет поле в середину экспортируемой структуры `PluginConfig` и пересобирает только библиотеку. Проведи review границы совместимости.
assertions: establishes that an explicit ABI contract applies
identifies the exported layout change as a compatibility risk or defect
checks consumers, headers, compiler configuration, and versioning rather than relying only on the type name
proposes an ABI-focused verification or compatible representation

cases.prompt: A C++ library builds from its source tree and its in-tree tests pass. A clean external consumer installs the package and then fails at `find_package()` because an exported target refers to a required transitive dependency that the install tree does not provide. Review the failure and propose the smallest evidence-based next step.
assertions: does not treat the successful in-tree build as proof that the installed consumer contract works
inspects installed public headers, exported CMake targets, link interfaces, and transitive dependency ownership
proposes reproducing the failure from a separate consumer rather than adding arbitrary include_directories
distinguishes a package/export defect from an unestablished dependency contract

cases.prompt: A project is configured with the Visual Studio generator. The review request says to repair its Release build by adding `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` to the existing configure command. The Debug build is present and the project uses the generator's named configurations. What should the review establish before changing the command?
assertions: recognizes Visual Studio as a multi-config generator
does not prescribe CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE as the configuration selector for this generator
uses the generator-appropriate `--config Release` build and test path
keeps single-config guidance conditional on the actual generator

cases.prompt: Two repository components each bring a different pinned copy of the same C++ dependency and expose colliding CMake targets. The core library needs only one of them; an optional adapter currently discovers the other through its own submodule. Review the situation before deleting either checkout.
assertions: identifies dependency acquisition and version ownership as the first contract to establish
checks the CMake target graph and whether the core really depends on the optional adapter dependency
examines compatibility and a single authoritative provider before proposing consolidation
does not delete a submodule merely because its directory is duplicated

cases.prompt: A library uses `include/` for public headers and `src/` for implementations. Its installed package, exported targets, clean consumer, and declared C++ standard all work. A reviewer prefers colocating every `.hpp` beside its `.cpp` and asks for a migration before accepting the change. How should the review handle that request?
assertions: does not treat one source layout as a universal C++ requirement
accepts the existing layout when the public and installed consumer contracts are verified
asks for a concrete build, interface, or maintenance invariant before requiring migration
separates repository convention from API and package correctness
